column1: # Custom property-id registry - single authority for FORK-allocated property enum ids.
# Reserve an id here BEFORE the code that uses it lands. Two branches claiming the same id then
# collide as a git conflict in this file instead of as a silent post-merge duplicate.
# Motivating case: PropertyInt 9032 was claimed twice on the same day (PR #222 vs
# feature/equipment-mods). CI's duplicate-id test catches that only AFTER both sides merge.
# Flow: Docs/Runbook.md, "Reserving a custom property id".
#   status=reserved -> claimed, the code is not on master yet, so the enum member need not exist.
#                      If it DOES exist it must still name-match, so a reserved row needs no edit
#                      when its branch lands - only a flip to active once it is on master.
#   status=active   -> the enum member exists on master and MUST name-match this row exactly.
# A range row (id_or_range = "start-end") reserves a whole block and carries a block LABEL, not an
# enum name. It does not satisfy the per-id requirement: allocating an id inside a reserved block
# means splitting a single-id row out of it.
# Guarded bands: every enum member whose value falls inside a band below must have a row here with
# the exact same name. Enforced by Source/ACE.Server.Tests/PropertyRegistryTests.cs.
# Deliberately OUTSIDE the guarded bands, because these ids are not this fork's to allocate:
#   - PCAP recorder ids from upstream ACEmulator's packet-capture tooling:
#   - Upstream ACEmulator's own custom properties, which arrive here via upstream merges:
# Each fork band therefore starts one id past the last upstream allocation in that enum. An
# upstream merge that lands a NEW member inside a fork band fails the registry test on purpose:
# that is a genuine collision needing a decision, not a false alarm.
# Machine-readable band declarations - the test reads these lines, so keep them and the prose above
# enum_file is the enum name; the file is Source/ACE.Entity/Enum/Properties/<enum_file>.cs.
# Rows are tab-separated and sorted by enum_file (ordinal), then by id / range start.
